description: Declarative venue-access probe for Clean-Slate Night City. Compiled by tools/build-clean-slate.py into mod\neon_ascendancy\venue_probe.questphase and wired off ascendancy.questphase behind the dev fact na_dev_venue_probe > 0 (set only by NeonAscendancy_ApplyDevDebug). Each entry declares a venue's quest prefab, the door device actions that open it, and any community spawner activations. Venue phases carry prefabs, doors and communities ONLY - never journal, mappin, phone or street-story/gig phases (enforced by the builder). See docs/research/world-access.md section 4.2 Layer 1 and section 5.

venues.why: EP1 quest-only venue. The Barghest-logo shutters at the street entrance (~-1819,-2315) are the var_tower_gate_* decoration groups of #loc_q304_pr_combat_tower_decoration; the glass door behind them is #q303_dvc_combat_tower_main_door (owner look-at id 10339269932617277634, locked=true). Both the decoration and the door entities live under #loc_q304_combat_tower, so this phase must declare that prefab for the variant toggle and the device ref to resolve. Vanilla q303_07_finale declares only #q303_pr_combat_tower; the decoration/door node refs resolve because that prefab's questdesign tree sits inside the #loc_q304_combat_tower streamed prefab, which the location phase streams. We declare the location prefab so it is present regardless of story phase state. The garage backdoor is intentionally left sealed: its interior is unfinished previs geometry.

venues.why: The six EP1 fast-travel dataterms live in combat_zone_data_terminals_prefabLN6J6KI. Its host sector ep1/exterior_-30_-39_0_0 (and 6 others) declares combat_zone_data_terminals_active en=0 and combat_zone_data_terminals_deactive en=1, so the deactive shell renders. IMPORTANT: no vanilla questphase anywhere references this prefab - the toggle is world-streaming state, not a quest hook. #stadium_data_term_001 sits inside variant group index 1798 (the hidden active group), which is why the old proximity anchor deadlocked. The anchor is now an ungated decoration 3.6 m away. Whether a quest-phase variant toggle can flip a sector variant at all is exactly what the new debug facts test.

venues.display_name: Black Sapphire sneak-in route (q303 technical floor to floor 99)
venues.why: Vanilla q303_06b_paradise_technical drives the whole infiltration path with DoorControllerPS/WindowControllerPS/LiftControllerPS/PlatformControllerPS actions on these refs. We replay only the 'make it passable' subset (enable/power/unseal/unlock/open/on, lift power and floor access), behind one proximity wait at the tunnel entrance, and deliberately do NOT replay any ForceDisabled/ForceSeal/ForceClose/ForceLock step. Refuse/laundry dress and every scene stay out. Route: tunnel entrance door -> tunnels platform -> hatches -> tech-floor lift -> sniper gate -> tech-floor lift door -> laundry door -> floor 99. #q303_pr_combat_tower is declared by cast_and_hubs (Kurt's workspot), so it is omitted here to avoid a duplicate phasePrefab.

notes.summary: Dogtown vendors (stadium market + container_zone/monument_av/hillpark/high_peak/boulevard_av) are ep1\openworld\vendors\ep1_vendors.questphase, which our archive does NOT load. Its sub-phases are gated on ep1_side_content >= 1, and stadium additionally on q301_02_active > 0; each vendor zone also needs its *_default_on fact (e.g. cz_stadium_gunsmith_01_default_on) and models vendors as questSpawnSet/questCommunityTemplate nodes inside the location prefabs, not as questPrefabs of the vendor phase. Populating them therefore needs facts set at runtime (DevDebug), which the facts policy keeps out of the archive. Spawner refs verified in the phase: stadium #cz_stadium_black_market_01, _clothing_01, _food_01..03, _gunsmith_01, _junk_01, _medic_01, _netrunner_01, _ripperdoc_01 (entryName=<name>, phase A/None); container_zone #cz_con_{clothingshop,foodshop,gunsmith,junkshop,medicstore,ripdoc}_01; monument_av #cz_monument_av_ripperdoc_anderson, #farida; communities #cz_stadium_clothing_01_tommie_walker_com, #cz_stadium_ws_vendor_06_robot_com.

Afterlife back-room door (owner look-at id 17830752525230996744, app=doors_single_entropy_j, pos=(-1430.8,986.5,16.5), locked=true) is an anonymous/base-world door device; its authored ref was not resolvable from the offline extracts, so no unverified ref was added. Dexter: vanilla spawns him via questSpawnSet #dex entry='dex' phase='q005_afterlife_default' in q005_01_plan, which declares only #q005_pr_afterlife (no story prefab needed). His seat workspot #q005_ws_dex_afterlife_01 lives under the #q005_cin_01_plan sub-prefab INSIDE #q005_pr_afterlife, so declaring #q005_pr_afterlife in the cast layer and activating #dex/dex/q005_afterlife_default is enough to seat him with no scene/dialogue. Options if the cinematics sub-prefab is a problem: (a) declare #q005_pr_afterlife and spawn #dex as above; (b) use #q005_ws_dex_limo_afterlife (outside the cin prefab) instead.

Vanilla ep1\openworld\combat_zone_gate\combat_zone_gate.questphase declares #loc_q303_combat_zone_gate_openworld and drives the pedestrian checkpoint with DoorControllerPS ForcePower + ForceOpen (ForceUnpower/ForceClose to reseal). It is gated on ep1_side_content, q302_started, wanted_level, delamain_taxi_state, q304_block_dogtown_gate and dogtown_gate_combat_on. The pedestrian door NodeRefs are prefab-template placeholders inside loc_q303_combat_zone_gate_gameplay_prefab3JCC64Y (e.g. .../single_door_1_prefabCACGKLA/single_door_1_prefabMDLFXRQ); that prefab's sector was not extractable offline, so no unverified door ref was added, and the earlier census ids could not be hash-matched. Verified present: prefab #loc_q303_combat_zone_gate_openworld, triggers #combat_zone_gate_tr_inside / #combat_zone_gate_tr_entrance_to_cz_start / ..._to_nc_start, and the two ..._tr_entrance_foot_*_scan_close_door triggers (a proximity ref candidate). Also relevant: the combat-zone gate openworld sector is what a future pass should own so its device prefab streams; Dogtown access gate is separate from the Black Sapphire shutters.

Owner look-at: ElevatorFloorTerminal id=10896172302402141982, app=elevator_terminal_appearances_entropy_c, pos=(-624.755,796.916,133.703), powered=true disabled=false. That entity is inside the #q105_pr_dollhouse quest-design prefab, which is not a standalone streamed sector, so no authored '#name' for it could be hash-matched offline. Not added, to avoid inventing a ref. When it can be resolved, the sequence that works for the Black Sapphire terminal applies: AuthorizationDisable (or the terminal's own QuickHackAuthorization path, which sets m_authorizationProperties.m_isAuthorizationModuleOn=false and unlocks connected doors) - vanilla never issues a floor-unlock action on terminals, only ForceON/ForceOFF (q304_safehouse_elevator_scanner).
